Screen directions — research and alternatives for your call

For every screen: what it does today, what comparable apps do (with sources), and three materially different directions built from those aspects, each as a phone mock beside its wireframe and trade-off. Pick one per screen, or keep it, or say which parts to mix; your notes are saved for Claude to act on.

Decisions save on this device

Account, onboarding, profile, paywall, insights

Welcome + Sign in + Sign up /(auth)/welcome · /(auth)/sign-in · /(auth)/sign-up

Today: Welcome: brand mark, wordmark, one-line pitch, three tinted feature rows, 'Get started' (→ sign-up) and a secondary 'I already have an account' (→ sign-in). Sign-in: two-word heading, optional 'Sign in to join {household}' banner, Sign in with Apple, Google, email + password fields (username/password content types, return-key chaining), Sign in, 'Forgot password?', 'New here? Create an account'. Sign-up: heading + subtitle, Apple (SIGN_UP), Google, display name / email / password (8+), Create account; a refused sign-up that advises signing in shows a Sign in button. Cost today: Welcome→inside via Apple = 2 taps + Face ID; returning email user = 2 taps 0 keystrokes IF QuickType offers the pair (declared, needs the webcredentials build) else ~4 taps + ~32 keystrokes; new email user = 3 fields (~40 keystrokes, or ~25 + one tap for the suggested password) + 1 tap.

What other apps do (6 studied)
  • Notion (mobile + web) — One login screen for both new and returning people: Continue with Google / Apple / Microsoft, or an email field; email sends a temporary login code (and a magic link) instead of asking for a password; passkeys supported. Apple/Google work only when the email matches.
    • One door — no sign-in vs sign-up fork; the server decides from the email — Welcome's second button and the two mirrored screens exist only to route people; a single email-first screen removes one decision and one screen source
    • Emailed code instead of a password — Nothing to forget, so the reset flow disappears for most people source
  • Craft — Login screen lists email, Apple, Google, Microsoft, SSO. Email → a 6-digit verification code from the inbox; Continue with Apple asks whether to share the email; Hide My Email produces a relay address.
    • 6-digit code that iOS Security Code AutoFill can fill — Turns the second step into one tap on the QuickType bar rather than typing source
  • Slack — Open app → Sign in → choose a method: password, or 'Sign in with Email' which emails a confirmation code (or a magic link); SSO where required.
    • Code sign-in doubles as the recovery path — A person who forgot their password still gets in; password reset becomes an account-settings chore rather than a front-door flow source
  • Things 3 / Things Cloud — No account to start; the account is created from Settings → Things Cloud when sync is wanted: email + password → Continue → Terms checkbox → 4-digit emailed code → Continue.
    • Verification is a 4-digit code inside the app, not an email link that leaves it — The user never has to find their way back to the app; Ambry's reset link round-trips through Mail source
  • Duolingo — Value first: start → language → goal → placement quiz → lesson result → then 'create a profile' (age, name, email, password) mid-flow; account creation is skippable and re-prompted later.
    • Defer everything that is not needed to proceed — Ambry requires an account (spec 37 retired anonymity) but does NOT need a display name at sign-up — Apple supplies it and Profile → Your name already exists as the editor source
  • Apple HIG — Sign in with Apple, Onboarding, Password AutoFill — Button no smaller than other sign-in buttons and never below the fold; titles limited to Sign in / Sign up / Continue with Apple; welcome people immediately after Apple sign-in; postpone non-essential setup; QuickType offers the saved pair only for an associated domain with username/password content types.
    • 'Continue with Apple' as the one title on a merged door — The same button is valid for new and returning people, which is what a single screen needs source
    • Postpone non-essential setup; welcome immediately — Argues for dropping the display-name field and for no interstitial after Apple sign-in source
    • QuickType credential pair needs the association + content types — This is the 2-tap sign-in Ambry already declared; the design only holds once the webcredentials build ships source

Sign-in: two-word heading, optional 'Sign in to join {household}' banner, Sign in with Apple, Google, email + password fields (username/password content types, return-key chaining), Sign in, 'Forgot password?', 'New here? Create an account'. Sign-up: heading + subtitle, Apple (SIGN_UP), Google, display name / email / password (8+), Create account; a refused sign-up that advises signing in shows a Sign in button. Cost today: Welcome→inside via Apple = 2 taps + Face ID; returning email user = 2 taps 0 keystrokes IF QuickType offers the pair (declared, needs the webcredentials build) else ~4 taps + ~32 keystrokes; new email user = 3 fields (~40 keystrokes, or ~25 + one tap for the suggested password) + 1 tap.

A

One door

Welcome's single CTA opens one 'Continue' screen; the email decides whether you are new or returning.

Look for: One screen replaces Welcome’s fork and both forms: Apple, Google, one email field and Continue; the dashed block shows what appears after Continue for a returning address, the caption what a new one gets.

Regions
  1. Heading 'Continue to Ambry' (accessibilityRole=header)
  2. InviteBanner when a stash exists
  3. Sign in with Apple (Continue), then Google
  4. Divider 'or use email'
  5. Input email (username content type, clearButton, returnKey go)
  6. Button 'Continue' (disabled until an address)
  7. State 2, returning: password Input appears under the email (QuickType offers the pair) + 'Sign in' + 'Forgot password?' link
  8. State 2, new: password Input with newPassword + passwordRules (iOS suggests) + 'Create account' + one line 'Free to start. You can add your name later.'
  9. FailureNotice for refusals; unreachable → notice + retry; RATE_LIMITED shows the server's words
Borrowed
  • Email-first single screen (Notion)
  • Continue with Apple title, no scrolling (Apple HIG)
  • Name deferred to Profile (Duolingo / HIG onboarding)

Cost after: Apple: 1 tap + Face ID from Welcome (was 2). Returning email: 2 taps 0 keystrokes with QuickType (unchanged). New email: ~20 keystrokes + 1 tap suggested password + 2 taps (was ~40 + 1).

Trade-off: Needs a 'does this address have a password account' step — either a Worker probe (an explicit enumeration oracle; spec 28 §Hardening accepts sign-up as one already, bounded by the 10/min credential bucket) or Better Auth's sign-in-then-sign-up laundering. Decision for Everett. Removes the second Welcome button (agency: fewer forks, same reach).

B

Code, not password

Email → 6-digit emailed code, auto-filled by iOS; passwords stay for accounts that have them.

Look for: After the email, a six-box one-time-code field with iOS Security Code AutoFill offering the code above the keypad; “Use password instead” and a cooling-down Resend sit under Continue.

Regions
  1. Heading
  2. Apple, Google
  3. Input email + 'Email me a code'
  4. State 2: 'We sent a code to {email}' + one-time-code Input (textContentType oneTimeCode, numeric pad) + 'Continue' + 'Use password instead' + 'Resend' (60 s cool-down)
  5. Neutral copy on every address (no enumeration)
  6. FailureNotice; unreachable → retry
Borrowed
  • 6-digit code + Security Code AutoFill (Craft)
  • Code sign-in as the recovery path (Slack)
  • In-app 4-digit verification (Things Cloud)

Cost after: New or returning: ~20 keystrokes (email) + 1 tap + 1 QuickType tap + 1 tap; 0 passwords to invent or forget. Forgot-password disappears for code users.

Trade-off: Contradicts docs/adr/auth.md O2 (magic-link deliberately omitted for attack surface) — a PR-description escalation, not a silent divergence. Adds a Worker route (Better Auth email-OTP plugin) and a Resend template; an inbox round-trip per sign-in for people without a saved pair; enumeration-neutral copy required.

C

Two screens, two fields

Keep the fork; drop the display-name field so sign-up is email + suggested password.

Look for: The same sign-up screen minus the display-name field: email plus a password iOS has just suggested (“Use Strong Password” in the QuickType bar), Create account already live.

Regions
  1. Welcome unchanged (bordered secondary now exists via P1)
  2. Sign-up: heading + subtitle, Apple, Google, email, password (newPassword) — no name field
  3. Create account; refusal → Sign in button (as today)
  4. Post-sign-up: Profile's 'Your name' row is empty until set; Members list falls back to the email local-part
Borrowed
  • Ask only what is required up front (Apple HIG SiwA / Duolingo)

Cost after: Sign-up: 2 fields (~20 keystrokes + 1 suggested-password tap + 1 tap) from 3 (~40 + 1). Sign-in unchanged.

Trade-off: Smallest blast radius; keeps two mirrored screens (the duplication the brief dislikes). Needs a display-name fallback wherever a member is named (spec 17 already tolerates an empty name).

Forgot / reset password /(auth)/forgot-password · /(auth)/reset-password

Today: Forgot: in-screen title, optional expired/unusable notice, explainer, email Input (emailAddress), 'Send reset link' (disabled until an address), 'Back to sign in'; a sent request replaces the form with a mail glyph, the neutral no-enumeration sentence, 'Back to sign in' and 'Use a different email'. Reset (arrives by Universal Link, token held unexamined): title, one new-password field (newPassword + passwordRules), 'Set new password', 'Cancel — back to sign in'; success routes to sign-in with 'Password updated…' because Better Auth issues no session. Cost today: ~20 keystrokes (the email is NOT carried over from sign-in) + 1 tap → Mail → tap link → 1 tap suggested password + 1 tap → sign-in screen → 2 more taps. Three screens plus an inbox round-trip.

What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Slack — Sign in with an emailed confirmation code instead of the password; the password reset itself lives in Account settings → Password → 'Reset your password by email' (8+ chars).
    • Recovery = sign in with a code; password change is a settings task — Most locked-out people just want in; changing the password can happen later, signed in source
  • Apple Account — On a trusted iPhone: Settings → [name] → Sign-In & Security → Change Password, gated by the device passcode rather than the old password; borrowed device via the Support app; iforgot.apple.com on the web; account recovery last.
    • Possession of a signed-in device is the proof — Ambry has no 'Change password' inside the app at all — today the only route is signing out and using the forgot flow source
  • Instagram — 'Forgot password?' / 'Get help logging in' → enter username, email or phone → choose email or SMS → a login link or code; the link signs you in, then you may reset. Help page covers the not-received case (spam, wrong address).
    • Channel choice and a link that logs you in directly — The reset link doing the sign-in removes the re-sign-in step Ambry pays after 'Set new password' source
  • Notion — Email → temporary login code or magic link; a password is optional, so 'forgot password' is rarely reached.
    • Passwordless removes the flow — Same as Slack; Notion's version is the mainstream mobile shape source
  • Baymard / uxpatterns.dev (reset pattern) — Prefill the address from the sign-in field; tell people what happens next; keep requirements short; validate live.
    • Prefill from the sign-in field — The address was just typed one screen earlier — carrying it over is 20 keystrokes saved source
    • Avoid complex password requirements — Ambry's single 8-char floor is right; the suggested-password path keeps it invisible source
Now

Today

The request form as it ships: the email field is empty even though sign-in just held the address, the button is disabled until it is retyped, and the only way back is the link.

Forgot: in-screen title, optional expired/unusable notice, explainer, email Input (emailAddress), 'Send reset link' (disabled until an address), 'Back to sign in'; a sent request replaces the form with a mail glyph, the neutral no-enumeration sentence, 'Back to sign in' and 'Use a different email'. Reset (arrives by Universal Link, token held unexamined): title, one new-password field (newPassword + passwordRules), 'Set new password', 'Cancel — back to sign in'; success routes to sign-in with 'Password updated…' because Better Auth issues no session. Cost today: ~20 keystrokes (the email is NOT carried over from sign-in) + 1 tap → Mail → tap link → 1 tap suggested password + 1 tap → sign-in screen → 2 more taps. Three screens plus an inbox round-trip.

A

Reset lands you inside

Carry the address over, stash it with the pending token, and sign in automatically once the new password is set.

Look for: The address is already in the field and Send is live; the dashed block is the sent state with the new Open Mail button, and its last line is the point — setting the password signs you in.

Regions
  1. Forgot: title, email Input prefilled from sign-in's field (route param), 'Send reset link', 'Back to sign in'
  2. Sent state as today + an 'Open Mail' button (Linking 'message://') beside 'Use a different email'
  3. Reset: title, new-password Input, 'Set new password', Cancel
  4. Success: signInWithPassword(stashed email, new password) → pendingInviteRoute ?? '/' ; if no stash (other device) → today's sign-in notice
  5. Dead token → forgot with 'expired' notice (unchanged)
Borrowed
  • Prefill from sign-in (Baymard / uxpatterns)
  • The link that logs you in (Instagram)

Cost after: 0 keystrokes if the email was typed on sign-in + 1 tap; link; 1 QuickType tap + 1 tap → inside. Removes the final 2-tap re-sign-in and one screen visit.

Trade-off: Client-only: no server change (Better Auth still issues no session; the client simply signs in with what it holds). Amends spec 28 §UX item 3 (routes to sign-in). The stash is a plain email in AsyncStorage for ≤1 h — same class as the pending invite stash.

B

Sign in with a code instead

'Forgot password?' becomes 'Email me a sign-in code'; changing the password moves into Profile → Account.

Look for: “Forgot password?” has become “Email me a sign-in code”: the locked-out path is a six-box code screen, and changing the password moves to a row under Profile → Account (dashed block).

Regions
  1. Sign-in: link 'Email me a sign-in code'
  2. Code screen: 'We sent a code to {email}', one-time-code Input (AutoFill), Continue, Resend, 'Back to sign in'; neutral copy for every address
  3. Profile → Account → 'Change password' SettingsRow → TextPrompt-style sheet (current password not required when signed in on this device; Face ID optional)
  4. Reset-by-link stays as the fallback for old emails
Borrowed
  • Code sign-in as recovery (Slack)
  • Passcode/possession as proof for a change (Apple Account)

Cost after: Locked-out person: 1 tap + 1 QuickType tap + 1 tap, no password invented. Password change: 2 taps + typing, signed in.

Trade-off: Escalation against docs/adr/auth.md O2 (no second passwordless deep-link path). Needs a Worker OTP route + email template + a change-password route; the biggest win for the locked-out case of the three.

C

Passkey after first sign-in

Offer Face ID sign-in once inside, so there is nothing to forget next time.

Look for: A one-time tinted card at the top of Profile offers Face ID for next time; the Account group gains a Face ID sign-in switch, and the dashed strip is the unchanged sign-in screen’s QuickType bar offering the passkey.

Regions
  1. After first sign-in: a one-time card on Profile (or a toast action) 'Sign in with Face ID next time' → enrol
  2. Sign-in screen unchanged; QuickType offers the passkey above the keyboard
  3. Profile → Account → 'Face ID sign-in' SettingsRow (on/off)
  4. Forgot/reset flow unchanged as the fallback
Borrowed
  • Passkeys alongside password (Notion)
  • AutoFill surfaces the credential (Apple Password AutoFill)

Cost after: Returning sign-in: 1 tap + Face ID; the forgot flow is reached far less often.

Trade-off: Largest lift: Better Auth passkey plugin, WebAuthn RP on the Worker domain, and a native ASAuthorization module → a new EAS dev build (the §Decisions 5 class of change). Does not fix the locked-out case itself; pairs with either direction above.

Onboarding + first run + add household /(auth)/onboarding · /first-run · /add-household

Today: Onboarding: 'Set up your kitchen' + one-line subtitle; card 'Start a household' (Input prefilled 'Home', chips Home · Our place, 'Create household' live on arrival); card 'Join a household' (Input for code or pasted link, 'Join'); a 44pt 'Sign out'. First run (only after a fresh create): 'You're all set', one step 'Bring your household' (invite lives on Profile), footnote that Pantry/Fridge/Freezer exist, 'Start adding' → /add, 'Look around first' → /. Add household: ScreenHeader + the same two cards without the prefill. Cost today: create = 1 tap (+1 on first-run = 2 to the Add tab); join by pasted link = long-press → Paste → Join → confirm sheet Join = 4 taps; typed code = 16 keystrokes + 1 tap.

What other apps do (6 studied)
  • Bring! — Creating a list asks straight away whether to share it; an existing list is shared by long-press → 'Invite Friends' or ⋯ → Settings; the invite goes to the friend's Bring! email and is also shown inside their app on next open; participants are managed from the list's gear.
    • Sharing offered as a yes/no at creation time — Turns 'Bring your household' from an explanation into the thing itself, at the one moment it is relevant source
    • The invitation also appears inside the invitee's app — A second delivery channel that survives a lost email source
  • AnyList — ⋯ → Share, Email & Print → Share List → type an email; existing users get a push and the list appears; new users get an email to download and must register with the same address.
    • Existing users are added with no accept step — Counter-example to spec 43's always-confirm rule — right for an addressed invite, wrong for an anonymous link; keep confirm for links source
  • OurGroceries — One shared account per household: Settings → 'Share Your Lists' sends an invitation that installs the app if needed and signs the invitee into the same account; alternatively they type the shared email + password.
    • The invitation bootstraps install + sign-in in one step — Ambry's Worker fallback page already does 'get the app'; the missing half is landing the new install on the stashed invite, which spec 43 covers only when the link is tapped after install source
  • Apple Family Sharing — Settings → [name] → Family → Add Member → Invite People (Messages/Mail) or in person (they enter their Apple Account password on your device); invitee taps the invitation → Join; status and 'resend' per person under Family.
    • Invite in person — the joiner acts on the owner's phone — Two people in one kitchen is the common case; no link needs to travel source
    • Per-person invite status with resend — The owner can see who has not joined yet source
  • Splitwise — Groups tab → 'Start a group' is the primary path; members are added from group settings; a share link lives in group settings; joining happens from the link or by entering a code under 'Join a group'.
    • Create and join are not peers on one screen — Link arrivals never see Ambry's onboarding (they are stashed to the confirm sheet), so the Join card is serving only the typed-code minority source
  • Apple HIG — Onboarding — Postpone non-essential setup, provide defaults, keep prerequisite flows brief, make tutorials skippable.
    • Defaults over setup — The prefilled 'Home' already follows this; first-run is the remaining prerequisite screen source

A

Create is the screen, join is a row

One primary action and one quiet row; the join card collapses into a TextPrompt.

Look for: One primary action — the prefilled name, its chips and Create household — and joining demoted to a single chevron row; the dashed block is the TextPrompt that row opens.

Regions
  1. Title + subtitle
  2. Household name: Input prefilled 'Home' + chips (as today)
  3. Button 'Create household' (primary, live)
  4. SettingsRow 'Have an invite code or link?' (chevron) → TextPrompt with the paste field + Join; a pasted link routes to /join/<token> as today

  • Create primary, join secondary (Splitwise)

B

Share at creation

First-run becomes the invite: 'Who shares this kitchen?' with one Share button.

Look for: First-run is now the invite: “Test Home is ready”, a tile that says you are alone so far, one primary Invite button that opens the share sheet, and a bordered “Just me for now”; the toast is what follows a share.

Regions
  1. 'Home is ready' (largeTitle) + footnote about the three locations
  2. Tile row: household initial + 'Just you so far'
  3. Button 'Invite your household' → creates a spec-43 link (no limit · 7 days) and opens the share sheet
  4. Button (bordered) 'Just me for now' → /add

Delete first-run

Create → straight to Add, with a one-time toast carrying the locations footnote.

Look for: Creating the household lands straight on the Add tab; the toast carries the locations footnote first-run used to be a screen for, and the Profile tab wears a one-time badge until an invite is shared.

  1. Onboarding as today
  2. On create: router.replace('/add') + toast 'Home created · Pantry, Fridge, Freezer are ready'

Profile tab /(tabs)/profile

Today: LargeTitle 'Profile' over one long inset-grouped scroll: Account (Your name — inline editor; About you bio + links — inline editor; View my public profile), Household (switcher row → sheet with pencil-rename TextPrompt; invite-code row with tap-to-copy, Share, ⋯ Regenerate; Share invite link row → options sheet; Active links list + Revoke all; Leave/Delete household), Behaviour (two dependent switches + footnote), Learned shelf lives (list + Reset), Members (count, per-member ⋯), Notifications (Daily reminder switch, read-only Time), Plan (plan, AI-scans meter, Get/Manage Ambry Plus), About (Privacy Policy, Crash reports), an unheaded exit group (Sign out, Delete account), version, OFF attribution. Cost today: most rows 1 tap; Share invite link 1 tap → sheet → 1 tap; rename 4 taps + typing; the real cost is scrolling ~25 rows across 9 headers to find anything, and two inline save-model editors (name, bio) that S11 still counts.

What other apps do (6 studied)
  • Apple Settings (iOS 18) — Account card (photo + name) at the top pushing to the Apple Account screen; then grouped sections in order of use; search; each section has a short header description.
    • Identity card as a header that pushes — Name, bio, links and public profile are one object (the person) and can live one push away instead of as three top-level rows source
    • Most-used first, domains not switches at the top level — Profile's top level today mixes identity, a credential, switches, a meter and legal source
  • Apple HIG — Settings — Keep task-specific options in the screens they affect; minimise the count; defaults over configuration; a custom settings area holds only the rarely changed.
    • Options belong with the task — The two out-lifecycle switches are about the Out/grocery behaviour and could sit on that surface's overflow rather than in a global list source
  • Notion — My account — Photo, name, email → security (password, 2-step, passkeys) → log out of all devices → delete account near the end; preferences after.
    • Security-adjacent placement of sign-out-everywhere and delete — Ambry has no 'sign out other devices' and no in-app change-password; Notion shows where they belong when they arrive source
  • Strava — You tab — The tab is the person (activities, stats); settings are behind a gear: units, feed, privacy, notifications, subscription, integrations, credentials.
    • Person page vs settings page — Ambry's Profile is a settings list wearing a profile name; splitting the two is one option source
  • Overcast — Settings with a 'Nitpicky Details' section holding rarely-changed playback toggles at the bottom.
    • Rarely-touched toggles grouped last under an honest label — Behaviour + Learned shelf lives + Crash reports are Ambry's nitpicky details source
  • Instagram — Settings and privacy — Accounts Center pinned at the top; long settings list with search.
    • Search over a long settings list — Only worth it past ~40 rows; Ambry is at ~25 — a reason to reorganise rather than add search source

Account card + household hub

Two objects on the tab — you, and your kitchen — each one push away.

Join by invite /join/[token]

Today: Reached from a Universal Link (or pantry://join fallback). States: spinner 'Checking the invite'; dead link (glyph + neutral sentence + Close); unreachable (cloud glyph + ErrorState with retry + Close); already a member → toast + switch + home; signed out → token stashed, redirect to sign-in with the 'Sign in to join {name}' banner; signed in → a BottomSheet 'Join {name}?' + 'You'll share this household's pantry, grocery list, and expiry reminders' + Join + Cancel, floating over an empty grey screen. Cost today: 1 tap (happy path).

What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Discord — Opening an invite shows a splash: server icon and name, online and total member counts, then Accept Invite / No Thanks; some privacy settings can be adjusted before joining.
    • Show what you are joining — name, icon, how many people — A join is a commitment; the sheet today shows a name only source
    • Accept / No Thanks as two equal-weight exits — Ambry's Cancel is bare text; a bordered secondary now exists source
  • WhatsApp group links — Opening a link shows a preview with the group name and member count; the button is Join Group, or Request to Join when admins approve members; a QR sits beside the link; admins can reset the link.
    • Preview with member count before the button — Same argument as Discord, in a household-sized product source
    • Request-to-join as the owner-approval mode — Ambry's analogue is the use cap; an approval mode is a possible future spec, not a screen change source
  • Apple Family Sharing — The invitation arrives in Messages/Mail; tap → Join Family → sign in with the invited Apple Account → confirm what you share; the organiser sees per-person status.
    • Confirm step says what you will share and which account you are — Ambry's body line does the first; a 'Signed in as {email} — not you?' line would do the second, which matters because links are opened on shared devices source
  • AnyList — Existing users receive a push and the shared list simply appears — no accept step; new users register with the invited email.
    • A push notification carries the invite to a known user — For an addressed invite (not a link) the notification is the landing; Ambry has push already source
  • Bring! — The emailed invitation is also displayed inside the app on next open.
    • Second in-app delivery of a pending invite — Ambry's stash already does this for the signed-out case; the signed-in case could surface a pending invite on Pantry too source

Delete account /delete-account

Today: ScreenHeader 'Delete account'; red lead 'This is permanent…'; three cards: What gets deleted (4 bullets), What stays (2), Your subscription (+ 'Manage subscriptions' button); a 'Transfer ownership first' card appears on a 409 with the blocking households and 'Go to Profile'; prompt 'Type DELETE to confirm'; Input; 'Delete my account' armed only once the word is typed AND committed (Done/blur); footnote hint. No Alert (S12). Cost today: 6 keystrokes + Done + 1 tap ≈ 8 interactions; the keyboard opens on an irreversible screen.

What other apps do (6 studied)
  • Notion — Settings → your name → 'Delete my account' → a dialog lists which workspaces die with the account → type your account email → button 'Permanently delete account and N workspaces'; 30-day best-effort restore via support.
    • The button label carries the consequence count — Ambry knows which households die (sole member) and how many items they hold; saying '…and 1 household' beats a generic 'Delete my account' source
  • Instagram (Accounts Center) — Manage accounts → Deactivation or deletion → pick the account → Delete → reason picker → password → 30-day grace during which logging in cancels the deletion.
    • Password/identity as the gate, a reason as a control — The gate is a credential the person already has; no invented word source
    • Grace period, cancelled by signing in — Forgiveness (agency principle) for the one action Ambry cannot undo source
  • Discord — Password (+2FA) to confirm; the account sits 'pending deletion' ~14 days; opening the app in that window offers Restore Account.
    • Pending state with Restore on next sign-in — The safety net is on the sign-in screen, where a regretful person will be source
  • Apple Account — privacy.apple.com → Request to delete → review what happens → an access code is issued for tracking/cancelling; processing can take days. On a trusted device, security changes are gated by the device passcode.
    • Device passcode / biometrics as proof for a critical change — A Face ID prompt is a keyboard-free gate that is at least as deliberate as typing DELETE source
  • Apple — Guideline 5.1.1(v) — Deletion must be easy to find, must delete (not merely deactivate) the account and data, and must revoke Sign in with Apple tokens.
    • Grace periods are allowed only if the deletion actually completes — Bounds the Instagram/Discord direction: a pending state must still end in deletion source
  • iOS power-off slider — Hold side + volume until the slider appears, then drag 'slide to power off' — a drag/hold gesture as the confirmation for a consequential action.
    • A hold or drag as the deliberate act, not a typed word — A press-and-hold with a progress fill costs one gesture and no keyboard source

Hold to delete

Press and hold the button for two seconds; a fill shows progress; release early cancels.

Look for: The same cards, then one red button you hold for two seconds — the darker fill is the progress, caught mid-hold — with the footnote doubling as the VoiceOver hint; no typed word, no keyboard.

Regions
  1. Same cards as today
  2. A destructive Button with a 2 s hold (reanimated progress fill, haptic at completion), label 'Hold to delete my account'

Borrowed
  • Drag/hold as the deliberate act (iOS power-off slider)

Grace period

Deletion schedules; signing in within 14 days offers Restore.

  2. After confirm: signed out, toast 'Your account will be deleted on {date}'

Paywall (Ambry Plus) /paywall

Today: Empty ScreenHeader (back chevron) + LargeTitle 'Ambry Plus' with the usage meter as subtitle; lead sentence ('Everything you do by hand is free, forever…'); benefits card (checkmark rows from the server payload); either a 'You're on Ambry Plus' card + Manage subscriptions, or two radio option rows Monthly / Yearly (yearly preselected, savings badge, trial label only when the Apple Account is eligible), the 3.1.2 renewal disclosure ABOVE the CTA, 'Start free trial'/'Subscribe', 'Restore purchases' (secondary), Terms · Privacy links; a dark build shows the prices and a coming-soon line with no CTA. Cost today: 1 tap + the StoreKit sheet (Face ID). Price: the brief's decided figures are $4.99/mo · $29.99/yr · 14-day trial; specs/monetization.md, docs/adr/monetization.md D2 and STATIC_PACKAGES still say $2.99 · $24.99 · 7 days — the PR that changes the screen must move all three.

What other apps do (7 studied)
  • Apple HIG — In-app purchase — Show the total billing price per option; intro price, its duration and the standard price after ('1 month free, then $4.99 per month'); a way to restore; do not upsell existing subscribers; show the store only when payments are possible; use the system confirmation sheet.
    • One sentence: trial, then price — Ambry's disclosure already does this; the design question is what is loudest — the billed price must be source
  • App Review 3.1.2 (via RevenueCat's rejection guide) — Price, duration and renewal terms plus Terms/Privacy links on the purchase surface; rejections when the free trial is more conspicuous than the billed amount; restore required.
    • Billed price more prominent than the trial — Today the savings badge and 'Start free trial' are louder than '$29.99 per year' source
  • Bear Pro — $2.99/mo or $29.99/yr with a 7-day trial on both; the subscribe surface is a 'Bear Pro' header inside Settings; concrete feature nouns (sync, encryption, export, themes, OCR); one subscription covers all devices on the Apple ID.
    • The sale lives in Settings as a header card — The Plan group in Profile could be the paywall for the browsing case, leaving the full screen for the quota-exhausted moment source
    • Concrete nouns, same price shape as Ambry's decided one — Bear's $29.99/yr is the exact figure decided for Ambry — a familiar anchor source
  • Fantastical Premium — Individual and Family (up to 5) plans, 14-day trial without a card, feature list (scheduling, calendar sets, conferencing, Watch).
    • Family plan beside individual — A household app selling per-user Plus should at least say how a household is covered (spec 23 §4a left Family Sharing OFF for v1 — the paywall should state the answer either way) source
    • 14-day trial — Matches the decided trial length; Fantastical is the precedent for 14 over 7 source
  • CARROT Weather — Three tiers (Premium / Premium Ultra / Premium Family) with a feature comparison and a 7-day trial.
    • Free-vs-paid comparison as the persuasion — Ambry's story is 'everything by hand is free'; a two-column comparison says it in one glance source
  • Flighty Pro — No free trial; weekly/monthly/annual/lifetime plus family tiers; the free app is usable; one headline benefit.
    • One headline benefit above the plans — 'World's fastest delay alerts' beats a checklist; Ambry's is the receipt camera source
  • Lifesum (anti-pattern) — Carousel of plan cards; greyed-out locked features and upgrade prompts throughout the free experience.
    • Do not gate with greyed-out features everywhere — Ambry's decided posture is three paywall entrances and no nags source

Pantry overview tab src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx

Today: LargeTitle 'Pantry' (household subtitle only when the user is in more than one), an always-visible SearchField, an 'Expiring Soon' summary row whose badge earns its colour (neutral / orange / red) and pushes /expiring, then a 2-column grid of location cards (emoji glyph, 'N foods' or 'Empty', name) pushing /location/[id]; footer = bordered 'Add location' button + ScorecardCard. An all-empty pantry collapses the grid into one empty state with a tinted 'Add your first food'. Typing swaps the grid for a SectionList of matching items grouped by location, with the full ItemRow behaviour (chip cycle, out-toast Delete, trash). Cost today: 1 tap to any shelf, 1 tap to the expiring list; anything else (Low/Out across the pantry) needs a shelf plus its filter, or the keyboard.

What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Apple Reminders (home) — Smart-list tiles (Today, Scheduled, All, Flagged, Completed, Assigned to Me) each carrying a count, above 'My Lists' rows that also carry counts; custom smart lists filter across every list by tag, date, time, location, flag and priority; the search field sits under the large title.
    • Status tiles with counts as the first thing on the home screen, each a destination — Ambry's home surfaces one state (Expiring) and hides the other two the app tracks (Low, Out); Reminders shows that a count-tile row scales to four states without a menu source
    • Lists as rows with counts rather than cards — Rows survive eight or more locations and read as iOS; the card grid tops out visually at six source
  • Apple Home (Home tab) — A category row at the top (Lights, Security, Climate, Speakers, Water) that filters the whole home, then Cameras, Favorites, Scenes and Rooms sections of tiles; the ellipsis menu offers 'Edit Home View' (drag/resize tiles) and 'Reorder Sections'.
    • A filter-chip row of household-wide states above the tile grid — The states are the triage; the tiles are the places. Home keeps both without the states becoming a second screen source
    • Arrangement lives behind one ellipsis ('Edit Home View', 'Reorder Sections') — Ambry cannot reorder locations at all (spec 22 out of scope); Home shows the whole arrangement job fits one menu with a drag mode source
  • Grocy (stock overview) — A table of every product with amount and next due date, colour-coded by due status; the header carries status buttons with counts ('X products are overdue', 'Due soon', 'Below min. stock amount', 'In stock') that filter the table when clicked, plus location and product-group filters and a 'Clear filter' button; per-row consume/open/transfer/spoiled actions.
    • Summary counters that ARE the filters — Ambry's Expiring Soon row is a counter that navigates; Grocy shows the counter can filter in place, and that Overdue / Due soon / Below min are three separate counters, not one source
    • 'Due soon' includes today; overdue excludes today and tomorrow — Grocy needed three changelog fixes to get these boundaries right; Ambry's urgency() already encodes them and any counter must reuse it source
  • Sortly — Home shows a summary of item, folder and value totals with recent activity and low-stock notifications; folders and subfolders hold items; search and advanced search run across the whole inventory; the mobile tab bar is Workflows, Items, Search, Alerts, Menu.
    • Whole-inventory totals plus an alerts feed on the home screen — Ambry's home already counts per shelf; a household total and the 'needs attention' list are the two numbers a pantry glance wants source
    • Search as a tab-level surface across everything — Confirms spec 26's choice (search the whole pantry from the overview) is the inventory-app norm source
  • CozZo / NoWaste — CozZo's 'At Home' inventory has two views, 'All Items' and 'Spaces' (fridge, pantry, freezer, custom), with a 'Due Time' bar per item showing days remaining or overdue; NoWaste's home is a set of inventory lists (Freezer, Fridge, Pantry, up to six free) with counts, and each list sorts by expiry, name or category and filters by category or placement.
    • A single all-items view beside the by-space view — The question 'what do I have that is about to go' is pantry-wide; Ambry answers it only for the 7-day window, and only on a pushed screen source
    • Lists per storage with counts and an expiring badge — Direct peer of Ambry's card grid; the peers stack lists vertically rather than tiling them source

Location screen src/app/location/[id]/index.tsx

Today: ScreenHeader '🧊 Fridge' with one OverflowMenu (Edit location · Zones · Move all items to… · Delete location). List header: optional description, a once-per-device hint about struck-through rows, SearchField, then SegmentedControl All · Expiring · Low · Out beside Select (→ Select all / Cancel). SectionList: zone sections first, then fixed category sections (SectionHeader with counts); each ItemRow = tile, name (struck when out), 'added Sep 3', urgency badge, tap-to-cycle status chip (stocked → low → out, out pops a Delete toast), trash when out, long-press enters selection. Selection bar: count + Move (LocationPickerModal, undoable) · Pin (Alert of zones, only if zones exist) · Delete (one undo toast). Empty shelf → tray glyph + 'Add your first item'; filtered-to-nothing → magnifier + 'Nothing here matches.'; pull-to-refresh. What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Apple Reminders (a list) — Reminders inside sections that collapse on tap; the list's ellipsis offers 'Select Reminders', 'Sort By' (due date, creation date, priority, title), 'View as Columns' and list info; selecting shows a bottom toolbar to date, move, delete, assign, complete, tag or flag the selection; swipe right indents, swipe left deletes; completing is the circle.
    • Selection entered from the ellipsis, with the bulk verbs in a bottom toolbar — Matches Ambry's selection bar; shows the 'Select' word can leave the filter row for the menu without hurting discoverability, since long-press still exists source
    • Collapsible section headers — A shelf with nine category sections is a long scroll; tap-to-collapse is the iOS answer and Ambry's SectionHeader is not pressable yet source
  • Things 3 (a project) — To-dos under headings; swipe right on a to-do opens 'When'; swipe left starts a selection and dragging down the right edge extends it to many; tap-and-hold reorders; pull down in any list to search; the selection toolbar batch-acts.
    • One swipe edge for the scheduling verb, the other for selection — A gesture vocabulary that is the same on every list — the S3 defect (four row idioms) is what Ambry is still carrying on this screen source
    • Search revealed by pulling down, not a standing field — Ambry pays ~52pt of search field on every shelf, above the filter; Things pays nothing until asked source
  • Todoist (a project with sections) — Sections with tasks; swipe left/right actions are user-chosen from Complete, Schedule, Delete, Reminders (Select on Android); two-finger swipe selects a task; sections and tasks drag.
    • Swipe actions configured once in Settings, applied everywhere — If Ambry moves status changes onto swipes, a single household-wide rule beats per-screen strips source
  • Grocy (stock overview) — Status buttons with counts that filter the table (overdue / due soon / below min / in stock), location and product-group filters, a 'Clear filter' button, and per-row consume-one / consume-all / open / transfer / spoiled actions.
    • Filter buttons carry their counts — Ambry's four segments say nothing about how many rows each holds; 'Out 5' tells the user whether Select all → Delete is worth opening source
    • Per-row verbs are consumption events (consume, open, spoiled), not a status cycle — The chip cycle is a state machine the user has to walk; Grocy names the event that happened source
  • Apple Files / iOS Mail — Files: More → Select → tap items → bottom actions (Share, Move, Delete). Mail: Settings › Apps › Mail › Swipe Options choose the left/right actions; a full swipe fires the outermost action.
    • Full-swipe fires the outermost action — SwipeRow supports two actions per edge; a full swipe for the common one (Used / Out) makes the gesture one motion source
    • Select lives behind More, bulk verbs in a bottom bar — Same shape as Reminders; confirms it as the platform default for lists that mostly browse source

What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Apple Reminders (sections) — Sections are managed inside the list: New Section from the ellipsis, tap a section name to rename, touch-and-hold to drag it, tap to collapse, swipe left to delete; reminders not in a section sit under 'Others'; sections can be viewed as columns.
    • Sections are edited where they are displayed — there is no separate editor — Ambry's zones are the same object (a user-named group above the automatic ones) but need a push to a second screen to touch source
    • 'Others' holds everything unsectioned — Exactly Ambry's category sections under the zone sections; confirms the model and suggests the zone/category boundary needs no explaining source
  • Things 3 (headings) — Headings are created from the project's More menu or by dragging the plus button to the left edge; tap-and-hold a heading and drag it, and its to-dos move with it; to-dos move under a heading via swipe-select then Move; a finished heading is archived with its to-dos.
    • Create in place by dragging the + to the edge; the heading carries its rows when dragged — Reorder as the whole group is what Ambry's drag already does; creation in place is the missing half source
    • Move items under a heading from the selection toolbar — Ambry's multiselect Pin is this exactly; validates keeping pinning on the location screen source
  • Apple Notes (folders) — Touch and hold a folder → Rename or Delete; drag a folder to move it or onto another folder to nest; swipe left to delete.
    • Rename through a context action, not a live text field — A list of always-editable fields is what the critique flagged ('no cue that names are editable'); Notes shows the alternative the platform uses source
  • Trello (lists) — Tap a list title to edit it in place; drag lists to reorder; the list menu offers Move list, Copy list, Archive this list, Sort by, Set list limits, Change list color; lists collapse.
    • Title edits in place on tap; everything else in the list's menu — The split Ambry wants: a single-tap rename with no permanent field, and rarely-used actions out of the row source
  • iOS edit mode (HIG) / Apple Home 'Reorder Sections' — On iOS a table enters an edit mode before rows can be selected, reordered or deleted; reorder controls and delete controls appear per row. Home's 'Reorder Sections' is that mode applied to sections: drag the handle beside each, then Done.
    • An explicit Edit/Done mode that reveals handles and delete controls — The current row shows a trash and a handle permanently beside a live text field; edit mode separates reading from arranging source
    • Section reorder as a dedicated mode with drag handles — Same gesture Ambry ships, framed as a mode a user opts into source

  4. Pin mode (opened from the selection bar's Pin): the same rows without handles/×, a check on the current zone, 'Unpin' row when any selection is pinned, footer 'Edit zones' switching modes; replaces promptZone's Alert (which caps at ~6 buttons)
  5. Cancel row always (rule 7: every row commits)
  6. Empty: 'No zones yet' above the add field; error toasts via failureMessage
Borrowed
  • Move selected items under a heading from the selection toolbar (Things 3)
  • Sections managed inside the list they organise (Apple Reminders)

Cost after: Pin = Select + rows + Pin + 1 tap (same), now with a real list; manage zones = 2 taps from anywhere on the shelf, no push; reorder 1 drag inside the sheet.

Trade-off: Drag-to-reorder inside a modal sheet that also scrolls is the hardest gesture pairing in the app (SwipeRow and the zones pan both note the scroll race); a sheet doing two jobs risks the S11 problem of mixed contracts. It retires an Alert-based picker that cannot scale past six zones.

Today: Pushed from the Pantry summary row (and the daily reminder). ScreenHeader with an empty title and a right-slot 'Add all' (tinted, cart) → every listed row onto the grocery list; LargeTitle 'Expiring Soon' + 'N items this week'; StaleBanner; one tinted body CTA 'See what you can make with these' → Cook tab. What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Apple Reminders (Scheduled / Today) — Scheduled groups reminders into Past Due, Today, Tomorrow, the rest of the month, then each later month; Today splits into Morning, Afternoon, Tonight; completion is a tap on the circle; swipe left reveals Delete (with Flag and Details), swipe right indents.
    • Completion is a visible tap target on every row, not a swipe — 'Used' is Ambry's most frequent verb and it is hidden behind a leading swipe; Reminders makes the equivalent verb one visible tap source
    • Past Due first, then day buckets that widen as they recede — Confirms Ambry's Overdue → Today → Tomorrow → dated ordering; the widening buckets are a model for a longer horizon source
  • Todoist (Upcoming) — A week strip, an Overdue section with a 'Reschedule' button at its top-right that re-dates every overdue task in one go, then one section per day; tasks drag between days; swipe actions are chosen from Complete, Schedule, Delete, Reminders; the scheduler suggests Today, Tomorrow, This weekend, Next week.
    • A bulk 'Reschedule' on the Overdue section — Overdue food is the section that needs the most decisions; one header action (snooze all, or mark all used) is cheaper than N swipes source
    • Drag a task onto another day to re-date it — Ambry's day sections are the same shape; dragging a row from 'Today' to 'In 3 days' would be a re-date without a picker source
  • Things 3 (Today / Upcoming) — Today shows anything starting or due today plus overdue items, with an optional 'This Evening' section at the bottom; Upcoming lists the next seven days separately starting with tomorrow; swipe right opens the 'When' picker (Today, This Evening, Someday, a calendar, Clear).
    • Swipe right opens a small picker rather than firing one fixed verb — Ambry's '+2 days' is one fixed nudge; the item screen already has four; one picker on the swipe would give the list the same vocabulary source
    • 'This Evening' — a second axis inside Today — Grouping by day is not the only useful cut; a by-shelf cut is the kitchen's own source
  • Apple Mail (swipe options) — Settings › Apps › Mail › Swipe Options chooses what a left and right swipe do; dragging slowly reveals the menu, a full swipe fires the outermost action.
    • Full-swipe fires the outermost action — Ambry's trailing edge holds +2 days (inner) and List (outer); making the full swipe fire the outer one is the platform default and needs a SwipeRow flag source
  • CozZo / Fridgely / Pantry Check — CozZo sends daily reminders for items that expire today, soon, are expired or need restocking and has a 'Cook Expiring Products' board ranked by how many expiring products a recipe uses; Fridgely colour-codes days left per space and lets Premium users widen 'expiring soon' to 15–30 days; Pantry Check has an Expiring Items screen sorted by alert type.
    • A user-set horizon for 'expiring soon' — Ambry's 7 days is a constant; weekend shoppers want 10–14 source
    • Recipes ranked by expiring-product count, linked from the expiring view — Validates the Cook CTA; suggests the count ('uses 3 of these') is what makes the link worth tapping source

What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Apple Reminders (details) — A grouped Details sheet: title and notes, Date (with Today / Tomorrow / This Weekend / Date & Time quick options), Time, Early Reminder, Repeat, Tags, Location, When Messaging, Flag, Priority, List, Subtasks, Images, URL; the same quick dates sit in the toolbar over the keyboard when typing a reminder.
    • Relative quick dates offered before the calendar, everywhere a date is asked for — Ambry now has four nudges on the item screen and one on the swipe; Reminders shows the same set reused in both places source
    • One grouped sheet of value rows with disclosure — The shape #173 adopted; confirms Location ▸ / Zone ▸ / Expires as value rows is the platform idiom source
  • Things 3 (When) — The When picker offers Today, This Evening, Someday and a calendar, with Clear; a field accepts natural language — 'tod', 'tomorrow', 'next week', 'sat 9am', '17d', '17d from jul9', '3rd wed jul' — and shows the interpreted date before Return confirms it; swipe right on a row opens the same picker.
    • Typed natural-language dates with the interpretation echoed before commit — Ambry's exact-date path is eight digits with no year shown; '12 sep' or '10d' is fewer keystrokes and self-checking source
    • The same picker from the row's swipe and from the detail — One control for a date, wherever the date is set source
  • Todoist (scheduler) — Suggestions (Today, Tomorrow, This weekend, Next week, No date), a scrollable calendar whose days show a load bar, a type-a-date field taking natural language up to 150 characters, and dates coloured red (overdue), green (today), brown (tomorrow), purple (later).
    • Colour-coded date text by urgency — Ambry's expiry value row is muted grey whatever the date; the urgency tone the badge uses could colour the value source
    • Suggestions + calendar + typed entry in one scheduler — The three date paths as one control rather than three rows source
  • Fantastical (natural-language input) — One field; the parser highlights the date, time and location parts as you type ('Haircut tomorrow at Quick Cuts 10am'), '/calendar' picks the calendar, 'task' makes a task, and when it cannot resolve a date the interface falls back to the picker.
    • Graceful fallback from parsing to a picker — A typed expiry that does not parse must not fail silently; Fantastical's rule is the fallback Ambry's masked field would need source
  • Sortly (item detail) — An item page with photos, quantity, min level, price, tags, notes and custom fields; 'Quick Actions' edit and update quantities without opening the editor; bulk edit updates names, quantities, tags, notes and Min Level across items; low-stock alerts feed the home screen.
    • Quick actions on the detail for the frequent write — Ambry's frequent writes (used, +days, add to list) exist on the list rows but only Status exists here; a visible action row closes that gap source
    • Min level as a per-item threshold behind an alert — Ambry has no 'remind me when low' per item; Sortly's model is the simplest version source

Now

Today

The camera card owns the screen; a scan is a haptic and a count, and the staged list lives on a second screen behind Review.

ScreenHeader 'Scan barcode', camera card (reticle, hint, torch), 'Enter number instead' revealing a digits field + Look up, scan bar ('N staged' · Review). Detect -> haptic -> Worker lookup (catalog -> OFF -> not found) -> success haptic + live count; toast only for unknown, duplicate or error (Add by name action). Basket survives leaving; denied card keeps the digits field and Review. Cost: 0 taps per product; a session ends in 2 (Review -> Add N); an unknown barcode is named later in the editor (open + type + dismiss).

A

2A Queue under the viewfinder

The review screen is a second screen for a list the scanner already holds; show the staged rows here and commit here.

Look for: The staged rows are the review: they queue under a shorter camera, newest first, an unknown barcode is named by tapping it, and Add 4 to pantry commits from here (held while a row needs a name).

Regions
  1. ScreenHeader
  2. Camera ~45% height: reticle, torch, 'Enter number instead' as an overlay button
  3. Staged cells newest first (GroupedRow: name or warn 'Name this product', location Chip, '~7d', tick); tapping an unknown row opens TextPrompt
  4. Footer: Add N to pantry (primary) · Review (secondary); primary disabled with the review's hint while a row needs attention
  5. Empty: full-height camera, today's copy
  6. Denied card unchanged
  7. Error: toast with Add by name
Borrowed
  • Queue under the scanner + Add to Inventory (Pantry Check)
  • Multi-Add temporary list (MyFitnessPal)

Cost after: Clean haul = 1 tap (was 2); unknown named in 1 tap + typing, no modal.

Trade-off: Two commit surfaces must share BasketReview's commit (extract it); the camera loses height on small phones; ADR D3 holds because the queue is the review.

B

2B Set the shelf first

Review-time location edits exist because the heuristic guesses per item; when one bag goes to one shelf, say so once.

Look for: A destination is chosen once on the viewfinder (Auto is the default) and every following scan is stamped with it; the count names the mode so a forgotten Freezer cannot go unnoticed.

Regions
  1. ScreenHeader
  2. Camera with an overlay SegmentedControl: Auto · Fridge · Pantry · Freezer (>4 locations -> a Chip opening LocationPickerModal); the mode stamps every following scan
  3. Scan bar reads '6 staged · to Freezer' while a mode is set
  4. Enter number instead / denied card / errors unchanged
Borrowed
  • Pre-selected action applied per scan (Sortly)
  • Scan modes (Barcode Buddy (Grocy))

Cost after: 1 tap per shelf change, 0 per item; single-shelf hauls need no review edits.

Trade-off: A forgotten mode misfiles a batch: Auto is the default, the count names the mode, and review chips remain.

C

2C Result card, camera stays live

Replace haptic-plus-count with a card carrying the fact worth checking.

Look for: Each scan answers with the fact worth checking — name, shelf and estimate on a card over the bottom third with Change and dismiss — while the camera keeps scanning above it.

Regions
  1. ScreenHeader
  2. Full-height camera
  3. Per scan a card slides up over the bottom third for ~2.5 s: photo tile · name · 'Fridge · ~7 days' · Change chip · ×
  4. Unknown: 'Unknown barcode' card with an inline Name it field
  5. Duplicate: card says so; error: card with Add by name
  6. Scan bar (count · Review) under the camera
Borrowed
  • Instant result card (Yuka)
  • Passive detection, tappable badge (Apple Camera)

Cost after: 0 taps per known product; shelf change 2 taps now instead of in review; unknown named now.

Trade-off: A card over the reticle fights framing on small screens; more motion on a one-handed screen; VoiceOver keeps today's announcement.

Receipt / photo capture (camera-first, AI parse, quota meter) src/app/capture/receipt.tsx

Today: ScreenHeader 'Snap groceries or receipt'; viewfinder with overlay Receipt | Groceries control, corner glyphs Photos / PDF, shutter; one meter line naming the binding allowance; preview (image, hint, privacy line, Scan receipt, Retake/Cancel); analyzing (skeleton rows, Hide, continues in background); parse stages into the basket and opens the review; zero-items, quota upsell, daily cap, permission and retryable errors each keep Retake / Choose another / Try this photo again with an honest cost note. Cost: Snap row (1) -> shutter (2) -> Scan (3) -> review -> Add N (4); the 5-15 s wait holds the screen.

What other apps do (5 studied)
  • Expensify SmartScan — Camera first; gallery bottom-left, shutter bottom-right; Rapid Fire shoots a stack of receipts in a row; details fill in afterwards and you carry on.
    • Shoot-and-go with processing shown elsewhere — The wait need not hold the screen source
    • Rapid Fire multi-receipt — Several receipts in one visit source
  • Dext — Single / Multiple / Combine modes at the bottom of the camera; Combine stitches a long receipt across up to 50 shots into one item; a Processing section tops the inbox while extraction runs.
    • Combine mode for long receipts — A supermarket receipt does not fit one frame source
    • Processing as a section of the list — Progress lives where the result lands source
  • Apple Notes scanner — Auto capture on edge detection; manual shutter; Keep Scan / Retake; add pages; Save with a count.
    • Count on the commit button; two verbs on a preview — Says what will be sent; edge detection itself is outside expo-camera source
  • Fetch — Frame squarely, shoot, then slide the camera icon into the circle to submit; green checks for store/date/total; X to retake; long receipts need several photos.
    • A cheap deliberate submit gesture — Keeps the quota gate without a third screen source
    • Several photos of one receipt — Long receipts are the common receipt source
  • Wave — Long receipts captured in multiple sections; bulk-upload up to 10; mark as reviewed later.
    • Multi-section capture — Confirms the pattern across a second product source

3A Long receipt as parts

A supermarket receipt does not fit one frame; the spec calls multi-shot 'a v2'.

Look for: Each shutter press shrinks into a Part thumbnail and the camera stays live for the next section; the PDF corner becomes Scan 2 parts, so a long receipt is one Scan and one charge.

Regions

  2. After the shutter the frame shrinks to a thumbnail strip ('Part 1'); camera stays live with an 'Add next part' hint

B

3B The shutter is the gate

For a camera shot the preview repeats the viewfinder; keep the deliberate gesture as the shutter plus a short undo.

Look for: No preview screen: the frame freezes for 2.5 s behind Sending… Undo, nothing leaves the phone until the window closes, and earlier shots queue as chips (7 items · Reading… · Couldn’t read · Retry); the privacy promise moves under the meter.

Regions

  2. Shutter -> frame freezes for 2.5 s as a chip 'Sending… Undo'; nothing leaves the phone before the window closes

The analyzing screen is dead time; the parse already outlives the screen, so let the wait live where the result lands.

What other apps do (6 studied)
